messages:
maya: Rolling nvidia-container-toolkit 1.11.0 -> 1.12.0 in eu-west-1 now, seeing ~12 GPU nodes fail to start GPU containers. Containerd logs show mount errors for /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 and missing libnvidia-ml, permission denied. Kube events show CrashLoopBackOff. Reverting canary pool now. @samir @jonathan 

samir: Ugh, that sounds like the mount propagation / bind flags change in the runtime. Can you drop kernel + driver + toolkit versions and a snippet of the containerd error?

maya: paste logs:
```
node: gke-gpu-eu-1-az3 kernel=5.10.92-100
NVIDIA driver=525.85.05
nvidia-container-toolkit=1.12.0
containerd: time="2026-03-18T09:14:32Z" level=error msg="failed to mount /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1: permission denied"
```

jonathan: That matches a change where toolkit switched to rprivate/rslave defaults for some mounts. Quick workaround: update the GPU daemonset to use hostPath with mountPropagation: HostToContainer (or Bidirectional) for `/usr/lib` and `/run/nvidia`. Example snippet:
```yaml
- name: nvidia-libs
  hostPath:
    path: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu
  mountPath: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu
  mountPropagation: HostToContainer
- name: nvidia-run
  hostPath:
    path: /run/nvidia
  mountPath: /run/nvidia
  mountPropagation: Bidirectional
```
This avoids relying on the toolkit doing the bind with specific propagation.

lee: Autoscaler already started cordoning some older nodes and new nodes without the old toolkit are coming up, queue depth spiked ~40%. I'm pausing scale-down and moved critical jobs to a fallback pool in us-central. If we change the daemonset we should patch canary first.

maya: Rolling back toolkit to 1.11.0 on the canary nodepool now (started at 09:22 UTC). Filed issue with upstream: https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-docker/issues/5789 (internal ref INFRA-3221).

samir: If rollback doesn't clear it, another low-risk fix is to add shared mounts at the runtime config level. On hosts, add to `/etc/docker/daemon.json` or containerd config something like "runtimes": {"nvidia": {"options": {"mounts": ["/run/nvidia:/run/nvidia:shared"]}}} or add the equivalent in the toolkit config so the runtime creates shared mounts.

infra-bot: deploy-bot noticed rollback job submitted for nodepool gke-gpu-eu-canary at 1869124000 (job id dp-2026-03-18-09-26).

opsbot: incident INFRA-3221 created and paged oncall. Severity: P2. Current impact: ~12 nodes, ~40% GPU capacity in eu-west-1 degraded, some batch queues delayed.

jonathan: Also double-check dkms/kernel module versions; we've seen cases where driver 525 + kernel ABI mismatch surfaces similarly. `nvidia-smi` OK on host, but containers can't bind the .so into the namespace if propagation is wrong.

maya: Update: rollback finished on canary at 09:44 UTC, canary pods are healthy. Scheduling a staged rollback to remainder of eu-west-1 while we validate. Will keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:

samir: Thanks, good call. After we stabilise we should add an integration test that mounts a sample container with the new toolkit + typical host distro kernels to catch this.

lee: Agreed. Also opening an internal runbook note about mounting expectations and making mountPropagation explicit in our GPU daemonset to avoid relying on toolkit defaults.

maya: Closing loop later today after eu-west-1 finish. If anyone sees a stuck pod with `failed to mount` after the rollback ping here and include the pod logs.
